run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T04:14:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a short outage of the payment service during a payment Deployment rollout. At 2026-11-15T04:05:15Z a new payment ReplicaSet (payment-54499f9786, Deployment revision 2) was scaled 0->1 and the only old payment pod (payment-55766d76b9-846r8) was killed at 04:05:18Z, but the new payment container (started 04:05:18Z) logged its first line 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' only at 04:06:33.571Z - about 75 s during which no process was listening on port 8080. The payment Deployment has no readiness, liveness or startup probe, so the pod was reported Ready at 04:05:18Z and the old replica was removed before the replacement could serve. Checkout consequently stopped completing payments after 04:05:18.755Z ('payment went through' absent until 04:07:09.471Z while '[PlaceOrder]' kept arriving), frontend-proxy's Envoy access log shows repeated "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 responses in that interval, and the spanmetrics error rate of frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans peaked at ~0.77 errors/s (2m rate) around 04:07:30Z before falling back to ~0.01-0.02/s. Almost all error spans in the window belong to that same checkout/payment path (checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder and oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge, frontend POST /api/checkout, frontend-proxy ingress/router frontend egress); payment itself reports zero error spans and processed charges normally once its server was listening. A separate, steady trickle of frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans with no matching egress or frontend/checkout errors exists both before and after the burst; its nature could not be identified (no trace data after 04:00:45Z) and it is the most likely reason the alert, whose expression is not readable from Prometheus here, was still reporting a small nonzero rate at 04:14:53Z.

claims.text: frontend-proxy has exactly two span operations: 'ingress' (span_kind server) and 'router frontend egress' (client), and its only traces_span_metrics_calls_total series in 03:14:53Z-04:31:40Z are those two operations with status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET and STATUS_CODE_ERROR.

Over 03:14:53Z-04:31:40Z frontend-proxy accumulated about 89.2 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans on 'ingress' and 69.9 on 'router frontend egress', against about 26232 and 26249 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans on the same two operations respectively (span counts, not request counts).

The frontend-proxy 'ingress' error rate was near zero before 04:06:30Z (0-0.0148 errors/s at 2m resolution from 03:55Z), jumped to 0.322/s, 0.767/s, 0.444/s and 0.456/s at the 04:06:30Z-04:08:30Z evaluation points, and dropped back to 0.0118/s by 04:09:00Z, with 0-0.033/s afterwards.

The frontend-proxy Envoy access log shows the 5xx responses are predominantly checkout requests: e.g. "POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream with a 21-byte response body at 04:05:43.473Z, 04:05:46.425Z, 04:06:00.035Z ... through 04:07:02.874Z, and one 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} for "GET /api/products/66VCHSJNUP" at 04:07:27.903Z.

In the 76m47s window the error spans form one checkout/payment chain: checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 42.4 and checkout oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 42.5, frontend POST 69.9, frontend POST /api/checkout 69.9, frontend 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' 69.9, frontend grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 69.9, frontend-proxy ingress 89.2 and router frontend egress 69.9; in the 6-minute burst window 04:05:40Z-04:11:40Z the same series read 44.7/44.7 (checkout PlaceOrder and Charge), 44.7 for the frontend POST series and 45.8/43.6 for proxy ingress/egress.

payment was rolled out at 04:05:15Z-04:05:18Z: Deployment payment revision 2 scaled new ReplicaSet payment-54499f9786 (created 04:05:15Z) from 0 to 1, scaled old ReplicaSet payment-55766d76b9 (revision 1) from 1 to 0, created pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d (Scheduled 04:05:15Z, container Created/Started 04:05:17Z-04:05:18Z) and emitted 'Stopping container payment' for old pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 at 04:05:18Z plus SuccessfulDelete on the old ReplicaSet.

The payment Deployment (revision 2) defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe for container 'payment', uses image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment with CPU limit 20m / request 10m and memory limit 160Mi, and RollingUpdate with maxSurge 25% and maxUnavailable 25%.

The new payment container (pod payment-54499f9786-4r25d, started 04:05:18Z, restartCount 0, Ready condition true at 04:05:18Z) produced no log line until 'payment gRPC server started on port 8080' at 2026-11-15T04:06:33.571Z - about 75 seconds after the container started and after its predecessor had been killed.

Checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-h9bvp logged 'payment went through' continuously until 04:05:18.755Z, then no successful payment until 04:07:09.471Z, while '[PlaceOrder]' entries continued throughout the gap - i.e. checkout received orders but its payment step did not complete for about 111 seconds.

payment's own spans show no errors in the window: 'charge' 1341.8 spans and 'grpc.oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge' 1341.8 spans, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET, with STATUS_CODE_ERROR increase 0 for 'GET', 'dns.lookup' and 'tcp.connect'.

After its gRPC server started, payment processed charges normally: logs from 04:06:33Z-04:10:58Z and 04:14:13Z-04:14:59Z are pairs of 'Charge request received.' / 'Transaction complete.' with no error lines.

All 21 otel-demo pods are Running with restartCount 0; every pod except payment (startTime 04:05:15Z) and flagd (03:34:57Z) started 03:33:02Z-03:33:05Z, including frontend-proxy pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks. Across Deployments only payment and flagd are at revision 2, all others revision 1, and all report ready/updated replicas.

Outside the burst, frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans continue without any matching downstream error: 8.14 in 03:45:53Z-04:05:13Z and 8.61 in 04:10:40Z-04:31:40Z, while in those same two windows checkout PlaceOrder, checkout PaymentService/Charge, frontend POST and frontend POST /api/checkout, and frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' all show 0 errors.

flagd-related error spans in other services are a steady background unrelated to frontend-proxy: ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 3.05 over 03:14:53Z-04:31:40Z, fraud-detection 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 3.05, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 4.05, and comparable counts (1.02-2.04) in the pre-burst and post-burst sub-windows.

In the one available trace sample (spans starting 04:00:39Z-04:00:45Z), frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' spans are children of the same-trace 'ingress' spans and carry http.status_code 200 (plus one 308), so the proxy's client span is the call to the frontend service.

Primary cause: the single-replica payment Deployment rollout at 04:05:15Z removed the only serving payment pod (killed 04:05:18Z) while the replacement's gRPC listener was not bound until 04:06:33Z, and because the container has no readiness/startup probe the replacement was counted Ready immediately; checkout's PaymentService/Charge calls therefore failed, /api/checkout returned 500, and frontend-proxy ingress error spans (and hence RequestErrorRate) rose. This is the mechanism best supported by the timing and by the checkout-log gap, but no trace-level gRPC status for the burst is available to confirm the exact error code.

Secondary hypothesis for the alert's reported value of 0.0222 at 04:14:53Z (six minutes after the checkout burst ended): the alert keeps seeing the steady background of frontend-proxy 'ingress' error spans that have no matching egress or downstream error (8.14 per ~20 min before the burst, 8.61 per 21 min after). Their nature could not be identified, so whether they are genuine proxy failures or non-5xx spans marked error is unknown.

Why the payment application needed ~75 s from container start (04:05:18Z) to gRPC bind (04:06:33Z) is not established; the container's very low CPU limit (20m) is a plausible contributor to slow startup but is not verified by any measurement in this run.

payment was not returning error responses: its own spans have zero STATUS_CODE_ERROR in the window and its logs show successful 'Charge request received.'/'Transaction complete.' pairs from 04:06:33Z onward, so payment's contribution was an interval of unavailability (no listener), not a stream of failing RPCs - and the payment server spans do not show which callers broke.

Rejected: a frontend-proxy crash, OOM or restart as the cause. Pod frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-sznks is Running with restartCount 0, started 03:33:03Z, has no previous container instance, and its Deployment is still revision 1, so its error spans are upstream-caused rather than self-caused.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the flagd EventStream error spans in ad, fraud-detection and recommendation. They persist at similar rates in the pre-burst and post-burst windows, carry no frontend-proxy ingress error correlation, and their services show no other error series tied to the checkout path.

Add a readinessProbe (and a startupProbe) to the payment container that only passes once the gRPC port 8080 accepts connections, so the Service endpoint is not populated before the server is listening; alternatively set the Deployment's maxUnavailable to 0 and maxSurge to 1 so the old payment pod is not removed until its replacement is actually Serving.

Raise or remove payment's 20m CPU limit (or verify actual throttling at startup), and compare the payment Deployment revision 1 and revision 2 specs from Helm/change history to identify what the 04:05:15Z rollout changed, since the image tag is unchanged (2.1.3-payment) and the image digest could not be compared.

Inspect the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its evaluation windows outside this target, and classify the residual frontend-proxy ingress error spans that occur with no egress span (which requests/routes and which HTTP status they represent), so the alert can be tuned to the checkout-path failures instead of a nonzero-but-benign baseline.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules returned no rules at all for this target (both rule_name=RequestErrorRate and the unfiltered query), so the rule's expression, threshold (the annotation says 'above 0') and evaluation/for period - and therefore why it started firing at 04:14:53Z rather than during the 04:06-04:08Z peak - are unknown.

Change history is not an integrated data source in this run, so what changed in Deployment payment at revision 2 (Helm values / env / spec diff) is unverified; the replicasets expose the same tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-payment and the old pod was deleted, so the image digests of revision 1 and revision 2 could not be compared and a truly config-only change is not proven.

Jaeger returned no traces for frontend-proxy after about 04:00:45Z (searches for 04:06-04:09Z and 04:26-04:31Z came back empty), so the burst has no trace-level evidence of gRPC status codes, error messages, or the exact span hierarchy beyond the 04:00:40Z sample.
Logs of the deleted old payment pod payment-55766d76b9-846r8 are unavailable, so its shutdown behaviour and the precise time it stopped accepting connections cannot be checked.

The frontend service's container produced no readable log output in this run (0 bytes read for frontend-675fd7b5c5-zjtpt), so the 500 responses are evidenced only through the frontend-proxy access log and frontend span metrics, not through frontend application error text.

The access-log 5xx evidence is a limited slice: fetch_pod_logs returned only the newest 30-40 matching lines per call (lines_omitted was non-zero), so the exact first 500 timestamp and the total number of failed checkout requests are not established.

The nature of the ~0.008/s background frontend-proxy ingress error spans that have no matching egress span (and no downstream error) is unknown; without trace data for that period it cannot be determined whether they are real failures, non-5xx spans marked as errors, or proxy-level rejections.

Whether payment's ~75 s delay to bind port 8080 was caused by its 20m CPU limit, by an external dependency wait, or by something else is not verified; no CPU throttling or startup-timeout metric was queried.

Error series were not returned for cart, product-catalog, currency, shipping, email, quote, image-provider, kafka or otel-collector in the aggregated queries; absence of a returned series is not proof that those services had zero errors, so they are not certified unaffected here.
next_steps: Provide the RequestErrorRate rule definition and its 'for' duration so the 04:14:53Z firing time can be reconciled with the 04:06-04:08Z checkout error burst and the residual background ingress errors.
Retrieve the payment Deployment revision 1 vs revision 2 diff from Helm/GitOps or cluster audit logs to identify what the 04:05:15Z rollout changed.
Add a readinessProbe/startupProbe binding on payment's gRPC port and review the 20m CPU limit and the single-replica RollingUpdate settings for payment before the next rollout.

Classify the residual frontend-proxy ingress error spans (routes and HTTP statuses) that occur with no egress span, to decide whether the alert's '>0' condition should be tightened to checkout/5xx-specific errors.
